conventions.convention: Total variation is sup_A |μ(A)−ν(A)|, taking values in [0,1].

Processes start at n=0; conditional on the natural history through n, X_(n+1) has kernel P_(Γ_n). The family is jointly measurable, every fixed kernel preserves π, and each uniform adaptation size D_n is assumed measurable. Diminishing adaptation means convergence in probability.

Mixing times use positive fixed-kernel iterates, with infimum of the empty set equal to infinity. Their evaluations at the adaptive process are assumed measurable. Containment is uniform boundedness in probability over n for the specified initial law.
The common drift function V is finite everywhere and at least one; C has bounded V; minorization is one-step and pointwise, with ν_γ(C)=1 and common numerical constants.
Countable choice and dependent choice are explicitly assumed for the countable product supporting the rare-block counterexample.

load_bearing.statement: For an adaptive MCMC process, n≥0 and N≥1, Q_(n,N)(A)=E[P_(Γ_n)^N(X_n,A)] is a probability measure and TV(L(X_(n+N)),Q_(n,N)) ≤ sum over i=0,…,N−1 and j=0,…,i−1 of E[D_(n+j)], with empty inner sum zero.

For the jointly measurable common-invariant-target adaptive setup and a specified initial law, diminishing adaptation together with either simultaneous uniform ergodicity or containment implies TV(L(X_n),π)→0. This is a one-time marginal conclusion and does not itself assert a strong law, CLT, or sample-average convergence.

For probability kernels with common invariant π, a common finite measurable V≥1, measurable C with sup_C V≤v, and common constants v≥1, 0<δ≤1, 0<λ<1, b≥0 finite, assume each γ admits a probability ν_γ supported on C with P_γ(x,A)≥δν_γ(A) for x∈C and P_γV≤λV+b1_C everywhere. Then TV(P_γ^n(x,·),π)≤MV(x)ρ^n for all x, n≥0 and γ, where M<∞ and 0<ρ<1 depend only on v,δ,λ,b.
For the jointly measurable common-invariant-target adaptive process, D_n=sup_x TV(P_(Γ_(n+1))(x,·),P_(Γ_n)(x,·)) is assumed measurable; diminishing adaptation means D_n→0 in probability.
For every ε,δ>0 there is an integer N such that P_(μ_0)(M_ε(X_n,Γ_n)≤N)≥1−δ for every n≥0, where M_ε is the first positive fixed-kernel iterate within ε of π.
